run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T04:36:59Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by real error status on frontend-proxy spans: its 'ingress' spans carry error=true, http.status_code=503 and otel.status_code=ERROR, with nonzero 5-minute error increases in every observed point from 04:08:59 through 04:50:59 (values 1.11 to 10, peaking at 04:31:59-04:34:59), while its paired 'router frontend egress' client spans carry error="true" with http.status_code="0". The proxy's access log attributes these to '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' on upstream cluster 'frontend', i.e. the frontend side terminated the connection before any response started, and the failing traces contain no frontend server span. The frontend pod is Running/Ready with 0 restarts and deployment generation 1; its own error spans exist only in the 04:31:59-04:34:59 band (GET, POST, /api/checkout, one failed tcp.connect, two dns lookups), which coincides with the only workload change in the window, a product-catalog Deployment rollout at 04:29:34. The flagd ConfigMap declares productCatalogFailure defaultVariant 'on' while every other fault flag is 'off', but no product-catalog error evidence was observed, so it remains an unproven hypothesis; the sustained low error rate predates and outlives the rollout, so no single object is established as the origin and the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: frontend-proxy spans of operation 'ingress' carry error=true, http.status_code=503 and otel.status_code=ERROR in the traces returned for 04:06:53-04:24:38 (15 ingress rows, 12 of them 503/ERROR); the paired 'router frontend egress' client spans carry error="true" with http.status_code="0" and no frontend server span appears in those traces.

By 5-minute increase, frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR are nonzero in every observed point from 04:08:59 through 04:50:59 (1.11 to 10 per 5m), peaking at 9.36-10 for 04:31:59-04:34:59, while 'router frontend egress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR is nonzero only for those same points (peak 7.02).

The frontend-proxy container log shows 503 responses with response flag UC and detail 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' for requests routed to upstream cluster 'frontend' at 04:29:34, 04:30:28, 04:35:31, 04:36:02, 04:40:50, 04:44:18 and 04:45:04 (two lines); the pod has no previous container instance, i.e. it has not restarted.

Only these services have traces_span_metrics_calls_total series with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR in the window: accounting, ad, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, payment and recommendation; no product-catalog ERROR series is returned by the same aggregate.

The frontend Deployment is generation 1 with ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5; its pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, started 2026-11-17T03:56:32Z, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend, pod IP 100.96.3.42.

The frontend's own error spans are confined to points 04:31:59-04:34:59: span_name GET STATUS_CODE_ERROR 5.56-5.85, POST 1.11, POST /api/checkout 1.11, 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' 1.11, tcp.connect 1.11, plus dns.lookup 2.22 and tcp.connect 1.11 in STATUS_CODE_UNSET; all these series are 0 before and after that band.

The only workload change in the window is a product-catalog Deployment rollout: events at 04:29:34 'Scaled up replica set product-catalog-55f64b54c9 from 0 to 1' and at 04:29:38 'Scaled down replica set product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc from 1 to 0', with the new pod Created/Started 04:29:37 and the old pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-5spmp Killed 04:29:38 (ReplicaSet SuccessfulDelete).

The replacement product-catalog pod product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9 is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, started 2026-11-17T04:29:34Z, and its ReplicaSet template matches the previous ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc in container image, env (including GOMEMLIMIT=16MiB), ports, volumes and resources.

The ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) declares flag productCatalogFailure with state ENABLED and defaultVariant "on" (variants off=false, on=true), while every other fault-style flag it contains (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, recommendationCacheFailure) has defaultVariant "off".

At 04:25:29 the frontend's and checkout's client spans 'grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct' and 'oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct', and the product-catalog server span, returned rpc.grpc.status_code "0", and no span in that sampled trace carried an error status.
Service endpoints resolve: frontend -> 100.96.3.42:8080 (tcp-service), frontend-proxy -> 100.96.3.19:8080, product-catalog -> 100.96.4.33:8080, each with no notReadyAddresses.

At 04:40:00 an instant query for the ingress ERROR series of frontend-proxy (status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR) returned 0 while ingress STATUS_CODE_UNSET returned 0.0037 and 'router frontend egress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR returned 0, while the 5-minute increase series had shown nonzero ingress errors just before this point.

The mechanism behind the frontend-proxy error rate is that its upstream, the frontend application behind the 'frontend' cluster, terminates in-flight connections before sending a response, which Envoy reports as 503 with flag UC / upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}; the proxy starts the upstream request but never receives a response (upstream service time '-') and the frontend records no error span for most of these aborted requests.

The 04:31:59-04:34:59 spike (frontend-proxy ingress errors ~9-10 per 5m, egress errors 7.02 per 5m, frontend's 5 GET errors, 1 POST error, 1 /api/checkout error, 1 failed tcp.connect and 2 dns lookups) is plausibly explained by the product-catalog pod replacement at 04:29:34-04:29:38 (old pod IP removed while new pod 100.96.4.33 came up), i.e. transient connection-level failures during that rollout; this remains unverified because no retained trace covers that period.

The flagd setting productCatalogFailure="on" in flagd-config (ConfigMap flagd-config, key demo.flagd.json) is a fault-declaring candidate that cannot be excluded by name, but it does not match the observed failure path: the ERROR aggregate shows no product-catalog error spans, the sampled 04:25:29 GetProduct calls returned rpc.grpc.status_code=0, and the errors occur on frontend-proxy egress to the frontend rather than to product-catalog, so it is not established as the cause of these 503s.

The 04:29:34 product-catalog rollout is rejected as the explanation of the sustained frontend-proxy error rate the alert reports: frontend-proxy ingress ERROR increases are already nonzero in the earliest available 5-minute point (04:08:59, value 2.5) well before the rollout and remain nonzero after it (1.11-3.33 per 5m for 04:40:59-04:50:59), so the rollout can account at most for the transient peak.

Entities checked without failure evidence tying them to this cause: product-catalog pod product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9 is Running/Ready with 0 restarts; frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-chsmw is Running/Ready with 0 restarts on deployment generation 1; and the frontend, frontend-proxy and product-catalog Services list only ready endpoint addresses.

Read the RequestErrorRate rule from the Prometheus/Alertmanager instance that produced this alert to confirm the exact expression behind the reported value 0.01111111111111111, its threshold and any 'for' duration, since the queried Prometheus exposes no alerting rules while the observed frontend-proxy error ratio over its spans is far smaller.

Investigate the frontend's connection handling next: compare Envoy's upstream idle/keep-alive and max-requests-per-connection settings for the 'frontend' cluster inside the frontend-proxy image against the frontend server's keepAliveTimeout, and enable frontend request/error logging so the reason a request is aborted before response start is captured.

Pull change history for the otel-demo namespace to explain the product-catalog Deployment generation bump at 04:29:34 and to date the change of flagd flag productCatalogFailure to 'on'; the change-history integration is not available in this Run, so neither could be verified here.

gaps: The alerting rule RequestErrorRate is not loaded in the queried Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules filtered by rule_name=RequestErrorRate and by type=alert both returned no_data, so the expression that produced 0.01111111111111111, its threshold and any 'for' duration could not be verified.

Jaeger traces were retained only to about 2026-11-17T04:25:29Z (freshness ~2029s), so no trace covers the frontend error band 04:31:59-04:34:59, the product-catalog rollout at 04:29:34, or the alert start at 04:36:59; the internal spans of the failing requests are unknown.

The frontend container produced no log lines at all for 04:25:00-04:57:08 (fetch_pod_logs returned no_data with lines_read 0), so the application-side reason for terminating in-flight upstream connections is unknown.

Reads of the product-catalog and flagd pod logs returned no matching lines (product-catalog read 11,235 lines with none matching error|fail|panic|flag; flagd returned no_data), so absence of a logged fault in those pods is a limit of what was read, not proof of health.

The flagd containers (init-config, flagd, flagd-ui) produced no log lines for 03:56:00-04:57:08, so when and by whom productCatalogFailure was set to 'on' is unknown; the ConfigMap creationTimestamp 03:56:32Z does not date its data changes.

The change-history integration is not integrated in this Run, so the reason for the product-catalog Deployment generation bump (ReplicaSet product-catalog-55f64b54c9 created 04:29:34) cannot be determined; the surviving ReplicaSet templates are identical in container spec, so the changed field is not visible in current objects.

traces_span_metrics_calls_total data for frontend-proxy exists only from 04:06:59 to 04:50:59, so there is no baseline before the errors began and no reading after 04:51 to establish whether the alert condition persisted.
A query of NetworkPolicy objects in otel-demo returned no objects; because Kubernetes objects are only their current state, this cannot establish absence of policies during the incident window.

A cross-service instant query using a regex match on service_name returned no_data, so which of product-catalog and frontend-proxy were reporting spans at 04:55 could not be confirmed from that query.

No trace, log or metric explains why the frontend side terminates upstream connections before response start, so whether this is a keep-alive/connection-reuse artifact or an application abort remains unresolved.
next_steps: Inspect the RouteConfiguration/Cluster settings of the 'frontend' cluster inside the frontend-proxy (Envoy) image, especially upstream idle timeout, max requests per connection and outlier detection, to see whether Envoy reuses connections the frontend has already closed.

Correlate the exact 503 UC timestamps (04:29:34, 04:30:28, 04:35:31, 04:36:02, 04:40:50, 04:44:18, 04:45:04) with frontend process diagnostics such as server connection-close events, at human discretion.

Have a human review the flagd flag configuration owner and confirm whether productCatalogFailure is intentionally 'on'; if it is, verify the product-catalog code path it drives so it can be ruled in or out.
Confirm with the alert rule owner whether 'error rate above 0' with the current denominator is the intended threshold for a service showing this low-level background of aborted upstream connections.
